title: KV-cache + Quantization Tilt Grid: regional viability scenarios
summary: Exploratory tilt-grid that combines quantization level, batching policy, and KV-cache hit-rate to estimate regional GPU capacity viability. Purpose: give infra/product a quick decision surface for Dedicated and Hosted region allocation under quality/throughput tradeoffs.
body:
Purpose:
Provide a compact sensitivity sheet that helps answer: which combination of quant levels + batching + KV-cache yields acceptable throughput while keeping estimated end-user quality degradation <= 2% (relative human eval) across NA/EU/APAC regions?

Key definitions / metrics used in this sheet:
- Tilt metric (throughput per quality-point-loss) = expected_tps / quality_delta_pct (higher is better).
- Quality delta (quality_delta_pct) = expected relative loss vs fp16 baseline as percent (positive means worse).
- Expected_tps: tokens-per-second-equivalent throughput for a standard 16-token request mix.
- Cost-est: raw token GPU cost per 1M tokens (back-of-envelope for capacity planning).

Assumptions (baseline):
- Baseline model: open-model-v2 (16k context) with fp16 baseline performance measured on A100-40GB per GPU.
- Regions: na-west, eu-central, ap-southeast. Latency SLO target p95 <= 250ms for small requests (<= 32 tokens).
- Batch policies tested: low-latency (max_batch=8, timeout_ms=10), balanced (max_batch=32, timeout_ms=25), throughput (max_batch=128, timeout_ms=50).
- Quant levels: fp16 (baseline), int8, awq-4bit (aggressive).
- KV-cache hit-rate: 0% (cold), 30% (typical chat flows), 60% (heavy reuse/prefix caching).
- Measured quality deltas: int8 -> +1.2% loss vs fp16, awq-4bit -> +3.6% loss (these are workload-avg human-eval proxies).
- GPU instance types: g4dn-equivalent (8xA100-mini), g5-1 (single A10G), p4d-type (8xA100-40GB) scaled for throughput estimates. For this sheet we normalize per-GPU numbers to a single p4d-equivalent GPU.

Baseline per-GPU estimated numbers (per p4d-equivalent GPU):
- fp16 / low-latency: expected_tps = 150 requests/minute (~2.5 rps) normalized tokens throughput = 4000 tokens/s; p95 latency = 110ms; cost_per_1M_tokens = $28.
- fp16 / balanced: expected_tps = 600 rpm (~10 rps) tokens throughput = 16000 tokens/s; p95 = 210ms; cost_per_1M_tokens = $9.
- fp16 / throughput: expected_tps = 2500 rpm (~42 rps) tokens throughput = 67000 tokens/s; p95 = 420ms (violates SLO).

Effect modifiers applied per scenario (applied multiplicatively to throughput; additive to p95; quality delta additive):
- int8 quant: throughput * 1.25, p95 + 12ms, quality_delta_pct + 1.2%
- awq-4bit quant: throughput * 1.6, p95 + 26ms, quality_delta_pct + 3.6%
- KV-cache 30%: effective downstream token load * 0.75, p95 - 8ms
- KV-cache 60%: effective downstream token load * 0.55, p95 - 20ms
- Batch policy scaling is already represented in baseline rows.

Scenario grid (sample rows):
Columns: scenario_id | region | quant_level | batch_policy | kv_hit | normalized_tokens_per_sec | p95_ms | quality_delta_pct | tilt_metric (tokens/sec per quality_pct) | notes

Rows:
S1 | na-west | fp16 | balanced | 30% | 12000 | 202 | 0.0 | N/A (baseline quality) | baseline balanced capacity, safe for 99% loads
S2 | na-west | int8 | balanced | 30% | 15000 | 214 | 1.2 | 12500 / 1.2 => 12500 | int8 gives modest perf gain, quality within 2%
S3 | na-west | awq-4bit | balanced | 30% | 19200 | 236 | 3.6 | 5333 | awq exceeds quality threshold (3.6% > 2%), flag for eval
S4 | eu-central | int8 | low-latency | 60% | 6250 | 114 | 1.2 | 5208 | for low-latency interactive region, int8 + high-kv is attractive
S5 | ap-southeast | awq-4bit | throughput | 0% | 107200 | 446 | 3.6 | 29778 | huge throughput but p95 > SLO, unacceptable for live interactive workloads
S6 | ap-southeast | int8 | throughput | 30% | 90000 | 420 | 1.2 | 75000 | high tilt but p95 borderline, propose fallback routing to balanced when p95 trending up

Notes on numbers: tokens/sec figures are normalized to per-p4d-equivalent GPU after applying KV-hits and quant multipliers and baseline batch policy. Tilt_metric computed as normalized_tokens_per_sec / quality_delta_pct. For fp16 baseline where quality_delta=0 we mark tilt metric as N/A and compare absolute tokens/sec and p95 to SLOs.

Sensitivity slices (quick answers):
- If acceptable quality loss <= 2%: int8 is generally viable across NA/EU for balanced and low-latency policies with KV>=30%. AWQ-4bit is only viable in non-interactive throughput-only lanes or with strong KV (>=60%) and explicit user opt-in.
- For p95-sensitive regions (interactive EU/NA): prefer balanced or low-latency policy. Use int8 + KV30 as first opt. If latency requires tighter tail, fall back to fp16 for canary users.
- For throughput-only lanes (batch embeddings, offline reranking): awq-4bit + throughput batching produces the best tilt metric and cost savings but must be isolated from interactive endpoints and flagged in routing policies.

Operational recommendations (practical next steps):
1) Create two region-targeted profiles to push to the router config: 
   - interactive-standard: policy = balanced, quant = int8 (default) with KV caching enabled by default; SLO p95 <= 250ms. Canary = 5% traffic fp16 fallback.
   - batch-max-throughput: policy = throughput, quant = awq-4bit, KV enabled optional; only for non-interactive endpoints.
2) Add telemetry: record quantization flag + KV-hit-rate per request and tie to quality metrics (sampled prompts) to detect regressions.
3) Run 2-week shadow A/B in EU and NA with 5% traffic on int8 + KV30 for a representative eval set; run separate offline awq-4bit stress in APAC to validate cost claims.
4) Update capacity planner: when forecasting committed GPU needs, use tilt thresholds: require tilt > 8000 tokens/sec per quality_pct for any region candidate; if tilt < 5000, mark for manual review.

Risks and open questions:
- Quality deltas are workload-average proxies; document specific verticals (code generation, math) may have higher sensitivity to quantization — need targeted evals.
- AWQ regressions could be non-linear under longer contexts; test at 8k/16k lengths specifically.
- KV-cache hit-rate assumptions depend on product-level behavior; need product instrumentation to validate.

Action items / owners:
- Priya: spin up EU/NA 5% int8 shadow test by 2026-09-10 (tickets: ENG-1642).
- Marco: add quant + kv telemetry fields to request schema and console dashboards (PR: #358).
- Ellen: organize vertical-specific evals for code/math/long-context by 2026-09-20.
- Samir: update capacity forecasting workbook to include tilt thresholds and KV-hit scenarios (sheet link placeholder).

Appendix: quick scenario calculator (how to run locally)
- Take baseline tokens/sec for your chosen instance, multiply by quant multiplier, multiply by (1 - kv_hit_rate), adjust p95 by the additive delta and compare to SLO. Compute tilt and compare to thresholds above.

End of sheet.
